hints.title: Nibble Chunk Masking
hints.text: Every hexadecimal digit corresponds exactly to a 4-bit nibble. A 32-bit signed integer consists of at most 8 nibbles.

hints.title: Unsigned Bit Shift Mapping
hints.text: Mask the lowest 4 bits with hexadecimal 0xf to lookup the corresponding character, then shift the integer right logically by 4 bits.

hints.title: Negative Two-Complement Unsigned Mask
hints.text: If num is negative, treat it as num + 2^32 or use unsigned logical right shift (>>> in languages like Java and JS).

hints.title: See the blueprint

complexity.notes: Optimal solution achieving O(1) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Treating negative numbers with naive modulo arithmetic fails due to signed remainder conventions.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Masking with 0xFFFFFFFF handles two-complement representation in at most 8 nibble extractions.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should convert 32-bit negative numbers without calling language built-in hex formatters.
